items.title: Mcbee interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2020
items.q: we’re performing a tune by Arthur Blythe that I couldn’t find anything ever to do with that tune

ctx.x: He says, “If you’re soloing and you don’t feel like playing something, if you don’t feel comfortable with what you’re playing, play that.” Which means that given those special moments of practice, of study, that will come in, that vibe, that feeling of intent to be excellent will manifest itself somehow, even in the spirit of, you know — I tell my students, important is to after you play something if you don’t hear that, stop and look where you’re going because when you do that, stop. The spirit of it all of who…

know. And I said what the hell do I do? Here’s something I don’t like, I’m uncomfortable, and the people are like expecting the adventure of Cecil McBee. And what I did, I closed my eyes, literally, I just closed my eyes and went into my living room to where I usually would practice, and I played that. I put the tempo down and just played an open solo as though I would practice, and I ventured into this area and that area, and then I would balk a little bit, which would lead me into this you know, I really…
